paper_citation: Grosmark AD, Buzsáki G (2016). Diversity in neural firing dynamics supports both rigid and learned hippocampal sequences. Science 351, 1440–1443. https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aad1935
apparatus: one novel maze per session, between two sleep sessions in the home cage: a 1.9 m wooden linear maze (1.6 m stem), a 2.3 m metal linear maze (2 m stem) or a 1 m diameter wooden circular maze

archive.citation: Grosmark, Andres D.; Buzsáki, György (2026) Diversity in neural firing dynamics supports both rigid and learned hippocampal sequences (Version 0.261005.2101) [Data set]. DANDI Archive. https://doi.org/10.48324/dandi.000044/0.261005.2101

sampling_rate.source: the rate attribute of each DANDI 000044 file's position series (39.0626 Hz); the OSF file's timestamps step 0.0256 s. The Supplementary Materials' Methods state LED tracking 'at 39.69 Hz', 1.6% faster, which no file matches

position_span.source: the Supplementary Materials' Methods of Grosmark & Buzsáki 2016: a 1 m diameter circular maze, a 1.9 m and a 2.3 m linear maze; the largest span of the tracked positions must lie between 80% of the smallest maze (80 cm) and 120% of the largest (276 cm)

speed_limit.source: Iriarte-Díaz 2002, J. Exp. Biol. 205:2897-2908, Table 1: Rattus runs at most 13.78 body lengths/s at a 0.190 m body length, 2.62 m/s (from Garland 1983 and Nowak 1999); times 1.5 because the tracked point is a head-mounted LED, which swings faster than the body, and no source read states head speed

sessions.data_citation: Balzani, Edoardo; Broderick, William F; Viejo, Guillaume (2024) NeMoS Tutorial: datasets for the NeMoS tutorials. OSF. https://osf.io/5crqj/
sessions.verification: Checked by hand on 2026-11-03 against the file, its OSF metadata, NeMoS's place-cell tutorial (which downloads this file), the paper's Supplementary Materials, and DANDI 000044's copy of the session (sub-Achilles_ses-Achilles-10252013, read by byte range). File: its SHA-256 is the one OSF publishes for hu5ma. Units: 137 (120 pE, 17 pI; 65 lCA1, 72 rCA1), with the same ids, regions, cell types and 8,414,607 spike times, unit by unit, as DANDI's copy. Time: 12,847 position samples every 0.0256 s (39.06 Hz; the paper states 39.69 Hz) from 18,190.9 to 20,143.2 s, each a DANDI sample time to 5e-8 s, inside DANDI's maze epoch [18,079.5, 20,147.0) s; spikes from 0.036 to 34,861.1 s, inside DANDI's PRE, MAZE and POST epochs. Space: the position is the head's distance along the track's axis in cm (33.10 + 0.99975 x - 0.02299 y of DANDI's 2-D positions in cm, residuals at most 0.07 cm), 5.4 to 165.3 cm, a span of 159.9 cm against the stated 1.6 m stem. Trials: 84, each starting and stopping at a position sample. The file holds no epochs; the loader takes DANDI's.
